question: Two women are standing at a sink full of soapy water. One of them hands the other a plate that she has just washed. the second woman
options: throws the plate into the sink and starts to swim.
puts the plate on her head and walks outside to the garden.
turns on the oven and slides the plate in to bake.
dries the plate with a towel and places it on a rack.

question: A woman in a blue swimsuit is standing at the edge of a pool next to a child wearing arm floaties. The woman kneels and holds out her hands. the child
options: pulls the water out of the pool and hands it to the woman, who pours it into the floaties.
jumps off the edge into the water and the woman catches her and lifts her up, smiling.
takes off the floaties, puts them on the woman's feet, and the pool begins to roll away.
swims across the pool and the woman is standing on the bottom reading a book about arm floaties.

question: [header] How to remove a splinter [title] Wash your hands and the area around the splinter with soap and warm water. [step] This helps keep germs from getting into the skin. [title] Clean a pair of tweezers with rubbing alcohol.
options: [step] Hold the tweezers still and move your finger back and forth against the tips until the splinter falls out. [substeps] Do this for at least an hour.
[step] Dip the tweezers in the alcohol and press them deep into the skin to find the splinter. [substeps] The deeper you push, the less it will hurt.

[step] Grip the end of the splinter as close to the skin as you can and pull it out slowly at the same angle it went in. [substeps] If the end is not sticking out, you may need to use a clean needle to lift the skin first.
[title] Cover the splinter with a bandage and leave it in for several weeks. [step] The tweezers will heal the area on their own.

question: [header] How to care for a houseplant that is wilting [title] Check the soil. [step] Push a finger about an inch into the soil to see whether it is dry or soggy. Dry soil usually means the plant needs water, while wet, heavy soil may mean it has been overwatered.
options: [title] Bury the entire plant in the soil up to its leaves. [step] Cover the pot with a plastic bag and leave it in the freezer.
[substeps] If the soil is dry, water the plant slowly until water runs out of the drainage holes, then empty the saucer.
[substeps] If the soil is soggy, pour in more water to dilute it and then place the pot in a bathtub overnight with the lid closed.
[title] Paint the leaves green with a brush. [step] This will help the plant look healthier, and it will not need water.

question: A man is kneeling on a gym floor next to a large tire. he
options: takes a bucket of paint and sprays it onto the wall behind the tire.
wraps a rope around the tire and swings it over his head like a lasso.
lifts the tire onto his shoulders and walks it around the room while a woman records him.
grabs the bottom edge of the tire, pushes up with his legs, and flips it over several times across the floor.

question: Two men are in a small boat on a calm river. One of them is holding a paddle in each hand. they
options: paddle in rhythm, pulling the water back on either side as the boat glides forward past the trees.
set the paddles on fire and the boat begins to float up into the sky above the river.
fold the boat in half and put it in a backpack, then take a photo of the paddles with a phone.
both climb out onto the water and walk to the shore, carrying the boat on their heads like a hat.

question: [header] How to season a new wok [title] Scrub the wok with hot soapy water and a sponge. [step] This is the only time you should use soap on it, as it removes the factory oil coating. [title] Dry the wok completely and set it on the stove over high heat.
options: [step] Heat it until the metal turns a bluish-brown color, moving it around so the whole surface is heated. [title] Add a tablespoon of oil with a high smoke point and wipe it over the inside with a paper towel.
[title] Cover the wok with a layer of sugar and then set it outside in the sun. [step] The sun will make the surface black and shiny.
[step] Fill it with cold water right away so the metal cracks and forms a nonstick surface. [title] Repeat with more soap until it shines.
[step] Leave the wok on high heat for two days until the oil has completely dried. [title] Wrap it in a wet towel and put it in the sink.

question: A woman is standing in a kitchen with a large bowl of dough on the counter. She sprinkles flour over the surface and begins to knead the dough with both hands. she
options: cuts the dough into small squares and then throws them one by one at a wall to see which ones stick.
holds up a cup of coffee and pours it over the dough as she begins to speak to the camera about her day.
pushes the dough away with the heel of her hand, folds it over, and turns it a quarter turn before repeating.
puts the whole bowl in the sink and starts to wash the dough off with soap and a sponge.

question: [header] How to sharpen a kitchen knife with a whetstone [title] Soak the stone in water. [step] Most whetstones need to sit in water for about 10 to 15 minutes before use. Wait until the stone stops releasing air bubbles. [title] Set the stone on a damp towel so it does not slide.
options: [step] Press the flat of the blade against the stone and rub it back and forth until the metal gets very hot. [title] Dip the knife in oil to cool it down.
[step] Place the stone in the dishwasher on a low setting. [title] Remove the knife from the stone and cut the towel into thin strips.
[step] Hold the knife at about a 15 to 20 degree angle to the stone. Push the blade across the surface from the heel to the tip, as if you were trying to shave a thin layer off the stone.
[step] Hold the knife straight up and down so the spine touches the stone. Drag the handle along the surface until the stone is worn smooth.

question: A girl is standing in front of a large mirror in a dance studio, wearing a pink skirt. She raises one arm over her head and rises onto her toes. she
options: spins slowly in a circle, then lowers her arm and steps into another position, keeping her balance.
picks up the studio and carries it across the street, placing it in a parking space beside a car.
pulls her skirt over her head and the mirror begins to play music from a loudspeaker above the door.
sits down on the floor and begins to eat the mirror, one piece at a time, while the teacher watches.

question: A group of men in white uniforms are standing on a grassy field with long wooden bats. A man throws a red ball toward the one who is standing in front of a set of three sticks. the batter
options: drops the bat and hits the ball with his hat before the other men run off the field to eat lunch.
swings the bat and the ball flies across the field as the fielders turn to chase after it.
throws his bat toward the man and the grass turns red as the ball rolls into the sticks.
catches the ball in his teeth and the three sticks fall over onto the men in the white uniforms.

question: Two kids are at a table covered with newspaper. One of them dips a brush into a jar of water and then
options: wipes the brush on a paper towel and paints the newspaper white.
pours the water onto the table and drops the brush into the jar of paint.
swirls it on a small tray of watercolor paints and brushes the color onto a sheet of paper.
passes the brush to the other kid, who holds it over his head like a microphone.

question: A man in a red helmet stands at the top of a dirt track holding a bike. He pushes off and starts riding down the hill. he
options: stops in the middle of the track and begins polishing the pedals with a cloth.
pedals around a series of bumps and jumps, then slows down at the bottom.
leans back and flies up over the trees while the camera follows him.
turns the bike over and rides it on its seat to the finish line.

question: [header] How to paint a room [title] Prepare the walls. [step] Move furniture to the center of the room and cover it with plastic sheeting. Lay drop cloths along the floor so that paint does not drip onto it.
options: [substeps] Pour the paint directly onto the drop cloth so that it can soak into the walls overnight. Use a hammer to flatten any bumps.
[title] Hang wallpaper over the plastic sheeting, then paint the furniture the same color as the floor. [step] Leave the room for several weeks.
[substeps] Wash the walls with a damp sponge and mild soap, then let them dry completely. Fill any small holes with spackle and sand them smooth.
[title] Apply the paint to the ceiling with a spray bottle filled with water. [step] Wait for the drop cloths to dry before you take the furniture out of the house.

question: Two boys are in a backyard with a plastic wading pool. One of the boys fills a bucket with water from a hose and carries it to the pool. the other boy
options: takes the bucket and dumps it over his head, then they both laugh and run across the grass.
jumps into the pool and the hose is shown spraying the camera as the video ends.
turns off the hose and then drives away in a tractor as the first boy waves.
begins to mow the pool with a lawn mower while the first boy holds a tennis racket.

question: A woman is seen standing in front of a mirror holding a brush. She begins sectioning her long hair with her fingers. she
options: ties a section into a braid and continues working down the side of her head.
pulls out a pair of scissors and cuts the mirror in half.
shows the camera a plate of cookies and shakes it around.
dips the brush into a bowl of soup and then puts it in her mouth.

question: A woman is standing in front of a large window with a spray bottle and a squeegee. she
options: uses the squeegee to cut the window into small squares.
puts the spray bottle in the window and begins to climb inside it.
sprays the glass with the bottle, then pulls the squeegee down the window in long strokes.
sprays the squeegee and then wipes the window with the bottle.

question: A girl sits at a piano with sheet music in front of her. She places her fingers on the keys and begins to play a slow song. a woman beside her
options: takes the piano apart and carries each key to the other side of the room.
turns the pages of the music and nods along as the girl plays.
starts to play a trumpet through the lid of the piano and the girl hands her a sandwich.
stands up on the bench and begins to dance on the girl's hands.

question: [header] How to survive a long-haul flight [title] Choose your seat carefully. [step] Where you sit can make a big difference in how rested you feel when you land. Use the airline's website to look at the seat map as soon as check-in opens.
options: [substeps] If you want to sleep, pick a window seat so you can lean against the wall and nobody has to climb over you to reach the aisle. If you like to stretch your legs, an aisle seat is a better choice.
[title] Ask the pilot to let you sit in the cockpit. [step] Most pilots are happy to have a passenger sit up front during the flight, since it helps them stay awake.
[title] Pack a large suitcase and carry it on your lap. [step] Having all of your things within reach will keep you from needing to stand up during the flight.
[substeps] Sit directly beside the restrooms and the galley, because the constant activity will keep you alert. Passengers who try to sleep on a plane often wake up with a headache.

question: A man is standing at the edge of a frozen lake with a hand drill. He leans over and begins turning the drill into the ice. after several minutes, he
options: puts on a pair of skis and glides across the hole while holding the drill over his head.
pulls the drill out of the hole and drops a small baited line down into the water.
pours a bucket of hot soup into the hole and then walks away without looking back.
lifts the ice off the lake and carries it to a nearby boat where he plugs it in.

question: [header] How to make a bird feeder from a pine cone [title] Gather your supplies. [step] You will need a large pine cone, some string, peanut butter, and birdseed. Choose a pine cone that is dry and has its scales open.
options: [substeps] If the pine cone is closed, place it in the freezer until the scales open on their own. [title] Paint the pine cone with peanut butter and hang it in the oven.
[title] Tie the string around the top of the pine cone. [step] Make a loop at the end so that you can hang the feeder from a tree branch.
[title] Soak the pine cone in a bucket of birdseed for several days. [step] The seeds will grow into new pine cones that the birds can eat.
[title] Cut the pine cone into small pieces with a saw. [step] Mix the pieces with string and feed them to the birds one at a time.

question: [header] How to cook rice on the stove [title] Rinse the rice. [step] Put 1 cup (200 grams) of white rice in a fine mesh strainer and run cold water over it until the water runs clear. This removes extra starch so the rice will not clump. [title] Combine the rice and water in a saucepan.
options: [step] Add 4 cups of water and turn the heat to high. Stir constantly with a whisk until all the water has boiled away.
[step] Cover the pan with foil and place it in the freezer for 20 minutes. [title] Remove the foil and fluff the rice with a fork.
[step] Use 2 cups (475 milliliters) of water for each cup of rice. Bring the water to a boil, then cover the pan and lower the heat to the lowest setting.
[step] Pour in a cup of oil and let the rice fry for ten minutes without a lid. [title] Drain the oil through a strainer and serve.

question: [header] How to write a cover letter [title] Address the letter to a specific person. [step] Look on the company's website or call the office to find the name of the hiring manager. If you cannot find a name, use a professional greeting such as "Dear Hiring Manager."
options: [substeps] Use a bright, colorful font so the letter stands out from the others. Print it on red paper and fold it into a small triangle.
[title] Write your salary requirements in the first line. [step] Add the names of your previous bosses and tell the reader what you disliked about each of them.
[title] Mail the letter to the manager's home address. [step] This shows that you are willing to go the extra mile.
[title] Open with a sentence that states the job you are applying for. [step] Then briefly explain why you are a good fit for the position.

question: A man is sitting on a stool in a barn with a bucket beneath a cow. He wipes the udder with a damp cloth and then leans his head against the cow's side. he
options: ties the cloth around the bucket and rolls it across the barn.
pours the bucket into the cow's ear and begins to sing.
squeezes the teats one at a time, and milk streams into the bucket.
lifts the cow by its tail and shakes the bucket on the ground.

question: [header] How to fold a fitted sheet [title] Hold the sheet inside out. [step] Place your hands inside two adjacent corners of the sheet, with the elastic edge facing you. Bring your hands together so that one corner is tucked inside the other.
options: [substeps] Repeat with the other two corners, so all four corners are tucked together. [title] Lay the sheet flat and fold it into a neat rectangle.
[title] Pull all four corners over your head. [step] Spin around until the sheet is wrapped tightly around your body and then fold yourself in half.
[substeps] Tie the corners in a tight knot so the sheet will not unfold. [title] Place the knot in the washing machine for another cycle.
[title] Cut the elastic with scissors. [step] Once the elastic is gone, the sheet can be folded just like a flat sheet, with no extra steps.

question: [header] How to make a cup of French press coffee [title] Heat the water. [step] Bring fresh water to a boil in a kettle, then remove it from the heat and let it sit for about 30 seconds. [title] Add the coffee grounds. [step] Spoon coarsely ground coffee into the bottom of the french press. [substeps] A good rule of thumb is about 1 tablespoon of coffee for every 4 ounces of water.
options: Fill the press to the top with cold milk and set it on the stove. [substeps] Wait for the plunger to pop up before you stir.
Pour the hot water over the grounds, stir gently, and put the lid on with the plunger pulled up. [title] Let the coffee steep for about four minutes.
Grind the coffee as finely as you can so that it turns into a smooth paste. [title] Press the plunger all the way down before adding the water.
Add a pinch of baking soda to the grounds so that they will float to the top of the press. [title] Pour the coffee into the kettle and boil it again.

question: [header] How to make a bookmark from a corner of paper [title] Cut a square. [step] Start with a square of sturdy paper about 6 inches on each side. If you only have a rectangle, fold one corner over to find the extra length and trim it off.
options: [substeps] Staple the paper to the page you are reading. Use at least ten staples so that it holds.
[title] Glue the square to the front cover of the book. [step] This will keep the bookmark from ever falling out of the book.
[title] Fold the square in half diagonally. [step] Crease the fold firmly with your fingernail so that you have a triangle with the long edge at the bottom.
[substeps] Keep the paper as thin as possible so the bookmark will be easy to bend. Tissue paper works best for this.

question: A woman in a green jacket is standing next to a horse in a dirt arena. she
options: lifts the horse's front hoof, scrapes out the dirt with a small metal pick, and then sets the hoof down gently.
pours a bucket of water over the saddle and rides it across the arena like a sled.
puts a saddle on her own back and the horse climbs onto a wooden stand.
ties the horse to a fence and begins to paint its hooves with yellow glue.

question: A boy stands on a diving board at the edge of an indoor pool. he bounces twice on the end of the board and
options: takes off his goggles and hands them to the camera.
falls off the board backward and lands on the lifeguard chair.
swims across the pool while the board stays still.
dives forward into the water with his arms stretched out in front of him.

question: [header] How to stay focused while studying [title] Choose a quiet place to work. [step] Look for a spot with few distractions, like a library or an empty classroom. If you study at home, pick a room where people are less likely to interrupt you.
options: [substeps] Invite all of your friends over to study together, and play loud music to keep everyone awake.
[substeps] Turn on the television and keep your phone beside you, so you can check it whenever you hear a message.
[title] Study for as many hours as you can without taking a break. [step] This will help your brain build up energy.
Make sure the space is comfortable enough that you won't want to fall asleep. [substeps] A desk and a chair with good back support are usually better than a bed.

question: [header] How to make a fruit smoothie [title] Gather your ingredients. [step] You will need about one cup of frozen fruit, half a banana, and a splash of milk or juice. Yogurt can be added if you want a thicker, creamier drink.
options: [title] Add the ingredients to a blender. [step] Put the liquid in first, then the soft fruit, and finally the frozen fruit on top so that the blades can pull it down.
[substeps] Place the banana in the freezer for a month, then throw away the fruit and drink the milk through a straw without blending.
[title] Put everything in a bowl and bake it at 400 degrees for an hour. [step] Let the smoothie cool before you slice it.
[title] Pour the milk onto the blender's base and plug it into the wall. [step] Turn the blender upside down and shake it gently.

question: [header] How to make a paper mache bowl [title] Tear newspaper into long strips about an inch wide. [step] Smaller pieces work too, but strips are easier to layer. [title] Mix equal parts flour and water in a bowl until it forms a thin paste. [substeps] Stir out any lumps. Add a pinch of salt to keep the mixture from molding.
options: [step] Drink the paste slowly so that the newspaper strips can go down smoothly. If the paste is too thick, add a little more flour.
[title] Pour the paste directly onto the newspaper strips and let them sit overnight. [step] The strips will form into a bowl shape on their own.
[title] Bake the paste in the oven at 350 degrees until the bowl is hard and golden. [step] Then tear the newspaper into strips and fold them into the oven.
[title] Turn an upside-down bowl over the paste and cover it with plastic wrap. [step] Dip each strip into the paste, then lay it across the bowl, overlapping the edges.

question: [header] How to jump-start a car with a dead battery [title] Park the working car close to the dead one. [step] The two cars should be near enough for the cables to reach, but they should not touch each other. Turn both engines off and set the parking brakes. [title] Clamp one red cable to the positive terminal of the dead battery.
options: [step] Leave the other red clamp hanging loose in the air so the electricity can flow into the dead battery. [title] Start the dead car first.
[step] Attach the other red clamp to the positive terminal of the good battery. [title] Clamp one black cable to the negative terminal of the good battery.
[step] Clamp the other red end to the negative terminal of the good battery. [title] Connect the black cables to the two tailpipes.
[step] Touch the two red clamps together to test whether they have a charge. [title] Lay the cables across the hood and wait.

question: [header] How to bleed a radiator [title] Turn off your heating system and let the radiators cool completely. [step] Bleeding a hot radiator can release scalding water or steam. [title] Find the bleed valve at the top corner of the radiator.
options: [title] Turn the heating system to its highest setting and open the valve all the way. [step] Wait until the radiator is too hot to touch, then go to bed.
[step] Pull the valve off with a hammer and pour a glass of water into the hole. This will force the air to the bottom of the radiator.
[step] Tape the valve shut so no air can escape and then bleed the water from the pipes. If the radiator is cold at the bottom, add more air.
[step] Use the key to turn the valve a quarter turn counterclockwise while holding a cloth under it. You will hear air hissing out, and you should close the valve when water starts to drip.

question: A woman in a pink headband is standing on a tennis court with a basket of yellow balls beside her. She tosses a ball up and swings her racket. the ball
options: hits the net, then the net hits her racket and she tosses it back into the basket.
bounces off the racket and into the basket as the net slowly rolls up.
stays in the air while she walks around the court and sits down.
flies over the net and she grabs another ball from the basket.

question: [header] How to wash a wool sweater by hand [title] Check the care label. [step] Look for the tag inside the sweater to make sure that hand washing is safe. Some wool items must be dry cleaned only. [title] Fill a basin with lukewarm water. [step] Add a small amount of mild detergent made for delicate fabrics and swish it around until it is evenly mixed.
options: Scrub the sweater against a brick until the stains come out. [title] Hang the sweater from a clothesline while it is still dripping wet.
Add a cup of bleach to the water so that the wool fibers will become soft. [title] Spin the sweater in the dryer on high heat.
Pour boiling water into the basin and drop the sweater in for an hour. [substeps] Hot water helps wool keep its shape and size.
Submerge the sweater and press it gently under the water for a few minutes without twisting or rubbing it. [title] Rinse the sweater in clean water of the same temperature.

question: A group of kids are gathered in a gym, standing on a blue mat. A boy in a white uniform bows to another boy across from him. the two boys
options: start to spar, kicking and blocking each other while a referee watches from the side.
pick up the mat and carry it out of the gym, then bow to the camera and sit in a car.
begin to dance around the mat while the audience throws balls at them from the stands.
remove their uniforms and fold them on the mat, then walk to the pool and dive in one by one.

question: Two men in wetsuits are standing on a rocky shore holding surfboards. They walk into the water and lie down on their boards. as they
options: paddle, the camera zooms in on a man in the sky who is explaining how the rocks were made into water.
paddle out, a wave rolls in and they duck under it, then continue paddling toward the open water.
reach the shore, they put on their wetsuits and fold the boards into small squares.
paddle out, the boards climb onto their backs and carry them across the rocks to the road.

question: [header] How to grow basil indoors [title] Choose a sunny spot near a south-facing window. [step] Basil needs at least six hours of bright light each day to grow well. If your windows do not get much sun, you can place the pot under a grow light instead.
options: [title] Water the plant with hot water every morning. [step] The steam will help the leaves grow thick and dark before the end of the week.
[title] Plant the seeds in a pot with drainage holes filled with moist potting soil. [step] Cover the seeds with a thin layer of soil and keep the pot warm until they sprout.
[title] Bury the whole plant in the soil up to the top leaves. [step] Only the roots should be visible above the pot.
[substeps] Paint the inside of the pot white so that the roots can see the light. Basil roots will grow toward the glass.

question: We see an opening title screen. A man is standing in a field holding a long pole. He runs down a path and plants the pole in the ground. he
options: hangs the pole on the wall of a house and sits down.
throws the bar to a dog and the dog drives away in a car.
lifts into the air and goes over a high bar.
waters the pole and waits for it to grow leaves.

question: A man in a swimming cap stands at the end of a lane in a pool. He puts on a pair of goggles and bends his knees. he
options: wades to the other side of the pool and starts to mop the deck.
climbs the ladder and sits at the top of the lifeguard chair.
dives into the water and begins swimming down the lane.
takes off the goggles and hands them to the lifeguard.

question: A man in a orange vest is on a ladder beside a house. He holds a long hose attached to a vacuum and moves it along the gutter. leaves
options: fly out of the gutter and the man paints the gutter with a roller before showing the finished work.
grow back on the tree as the man talks to the camera about how to bake a cake.
are shown being thrown onto the roof by the man as he laughs and climbs down the ladder.
are sucked up through the hose as the man slowly moves the ladder to the next section of the house.

question: Two men in helmets stand on a scaffold beside a brick wall. One of them lifts a trowel and scoops mortar from a board. he
options: spreads the mortar along the top of the wall and sets a brick into it.
throws the mortar into the air and catches it with the brick.
lays the trowel on the scaffold and starts to pour the wall into the board.
climbs into the board and the other man hands him a brick to eat.

question: A woman is sitting on the floor of a living room with a baby in front of her. She holds up a colorful stuffed toy and shakes it. the baby
options: turns the toy into a puppet and the two of them walk out of the room.
picks up a guitar and begins to play while the woman claps.
reaches out and grabs the toy, then puts it in her mouth.
stands up and carries the woman across the room.

question: [header] How to make a bed with hospital corners [title] Start with the fitted sheet. [step] Stretch the fitted sheet over each corner of the mattress so that it fits snugly and has no wrinkles. [title] Lay the flat sheet on top. [step] Line up the top edge of the flat sheet with the head of the mattress, leaving the extra length at the foot of the bed.
options: Cut the extra sheet away with scissors and throw it into the laundry with the pillows. [substeps] Hospital corners are made from the pillowcase and not from the sheet.
Fold the mattress in half so that the sheet is no longer touching the floor. [title] Staple the corners of the sheet to the frame.
Spread the pillows across the foot of the bed and sit on them for a few minutes. [substeps] This will make the sheet shrink to the right size.
Tuck the bottom edge of the sheet firmly under the mattress. [title] Lift the side edge of the sheet about 12 inches from the corner and lay it on top of the bed to form a triangle.

question: A man is sitting on a folding chair on a sidewalk with a violin tucked under his chin. A small crowd has stopped to watch. he
options: puts the violin on the chair and plays the chair with a small bow as the crowd slowly melts.
draws the bow across the strings and plays a fast song while a few people drop money in the open case at his feet.
pulls a second violin out of his chin and the crowd takes turns wearing the case.
stops playing and begins to eat the bow while the crowd turns around and plays the sidewalk.

question: [header] How to clean a cast iron skillet [title] Rinse the pan with hot water. [step] Do this right after cooking, while the pan is still warm. Use a stiff brush or a non-metal scraper to loosen any stuck food.
options: [substeps] Soak the skillet overnight in a sink full of soapy water so the grime softens and the iron absorbs the moisture it needs.
[substeps] If bits of food remain, scrub with coarse salt and a little water, then rinse again. Avoid using too much soap, as it can strip the seasoning.
Put the skillet in the dishwasher on the hottest setting. [substeps] Let it run through the full cycle, including the heated dry.
[title] Scrub the pan with a steel wool pad and strong bleach. [step] This will make the seasoning thicker and darker.

question: [header] How to keep cut flowers fresh longer [title] Trim the stems. [step] As soon as you bring the flowers home, cut about an inch off the bottom of each stem. Use sharp scissors or a knife and cut at an angle.
options: [title] Place the flowers in a hot oven. [step] The heat will open the buds and help the flowers last for several weeks.
[substeps] Use blunt scissors so that the stems are crushed and the flowers can not drink any water. This will keep the petals from opening too quickly.
[title] Remove all of the petals from the flowers. [step] Petals take a lot of water, so without them the flowers will stay alive longer.
[substeps] A slanted cut gives the stem more surface area to take in water and keeps it from sitting flat against the bottom of the vase. Do this under running water if possible.

question: [header] How to freeze fresh strawberries [title] Wash and dry the berries. [step] Rinse the strawberries under cool running water, then spread them out on a clean towel. Pat them dry gently so that they are not wet when they go in the freezer. [title] Remove the stems.
options: [step] Place the stems in a pot of boiling water and let them sit for about an hour. [substeps] The stems will turn red and sweet once they have thawed.
[step] Press the strawberries into the towel until all of the seeds have been removed from the fruit. Then pour the seeds into a freezer bag and store them.
[step] Use a small paring knife or a straw to cut out the green tops and the white core beneath. [substeps] You can leave small berries whole or slice larger ones in half.
[step] Leave the stems on and freeze the berries on a hot baking sheet. [substeps] This will keep the berries from sticking together in the oven.

question: Two men are standing on a basketball court. One of them bounces the ball a few times and looks at the hoop. he
options: jumps and shoots the ball, and it goes through the net.
kicks the net and a crowd of dancers enters the court.
throws the hoop across the court and runs after it.
